clue.text: Holding paper, cry "Everything for sport!"

indicators.note: the word for cry keeps the paper's letters held within it

parts.note: to sob is to cry
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
everything means all

explanation.surface: Someone clutching a newspaper shouts that they would give everything for the game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team bat-and-ball game, a close cousin of baseball, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: Parties want state welfare cut in half

indicators.note: only the first half of the long phrase for state welfare is kept

parts.note: social security is government welfare support

explanation.surface: Parties want welfare spending halved.
explanation.walkthrough: SOCIAL SECURITY has fourteen letters; its first seven give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal gatherings or get-togethers are also called by this name, a synonym of parties.

clue.text: In foreign land, man's democratic right

indicators.note: the man's word sits within the name of the foreign land

parts.note: France is a foreign land to the British setter
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: Abroad, a man claims his right to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote in elections, the basic democratic right.

clue.text: Handing out lots of cards doesn't impress me at all

definitions.meaning: a large deal, cards given out in quantity
an ironic exclamation meaning so what

explanation.definitionFit: Said sarcastically, the phrase dismisses something; literally it describes a generous deal of cards.

clue.text: Look cheerful, as one may with a cigarette

definitions.meaning: a face can brighten with joy

definitions.text: as one may with a cigarette

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to brighten in expression and also to ignite something for smoking.

clue.text: A lot of province included in Olympic venue

indicators.note: the province's letters are placed within the word for a lot

parts.note: a lot means much
NI is Northern Ireland, the UK province

explanation.surface: Part of a province is drawn into hosting the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of province' looks like one phrase, but 'of' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian city hosted the 1972 Summer Olympics, so it is an example of an Olympic venue.

clue.text: Front in Med is to weaken, admitting a break in the cloud

indicators.note: the combined letters let the next pieces in between them
the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ail is to grow weak or sickly
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean weather front weakens, letting a gap appear in the cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link; the insertion lands just after the M, not at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's tails are wispy cirrus streaks high in the sky, a type of cloud.

clue.text: Amphibian gets personal, specially-built dwelling-place

parts.note: a newt is an amphibian
own means personal, as in one's own

explanation.surface: An amphibian acquires a custom-built home of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: A New Town is a planned settlement built in post-war Britain, such as Milton Keynes.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned British settlements were built from scratch to house people, so a purpose-made place to live.

clue.text: Take responsibility for one short series of films

parts.note: to carry a burden is to take responsibility for it

indicators.note: the word one loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone accepts blame for one brief run of films.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long-running series of British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a famous British run of bawdy comedy films from 1958 onwards.

clue.text: Get shifting on the road —- could this create rage?

parts.note: read as an instruction to rearrange the letters of a four-letter word for kit or equipment, which produces the clue's final word

explanation.surface: A driver's gear-shifting on the road might provoke road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: altering the letters of GEAR creates RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers select a different ratio in the gearbox while moving, which is shifting on the road.

clue.text: Enthusiastic with weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to be armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a hearty, eager one, so the word is a synonym of enthusiastic.

clue.text: There's something very familiar in accounts of Roman empire

definitions.meaning: an idiom for news or a matter that everyone already knows well and is long past
the literal sense: the study of the classical world, such as Rome

explanation.surface: Something everyone knows sits in histories of the Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means old news, widely known; literally it is the study of antiquity such as Rome.

clue.text: Joint used in smack is one method of boat construction

indicators.note: the joint's letters are placed inside the word for smack

parts.note: to slap is to smack
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A carpentry joint is used in building a fishing smack, a traditional way of making boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' suggests a fishing boat to fit the surface; here it means a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping planks fitted with rebated edges form a hull method also used for wooden cladding.

clue.text: Thinking Greek has come up to ring Child Line

indicators.note: the word for come up surrounds the next letters as a ring does

parts.note: to arise is to come up
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker has turned up to phone a children's helpline.
explanation.walkthrough: ChildLine is a UK helpline for children; here 'Child' and 'Line' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous philosopher of ancient Athens was a Greek thinker.

clue.text: Declining to cross river, showing caution

indicators.note: the word for declining spans the river's letter, which sits within it

parts.note: waning means declining, like the moon

explanation.surface: Someone declines to cross a river, being cautious.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautionary sign or note gives notice of danger, so the adjective means cautionary.

clue.text: With sign of slight damage inside, harden and contract

indicators.note: the dent's letters go within the word for harden

parts.note: to inure is to harden or accustom
a dent is a small mark of damage

explanation.surface: A slightly damaged item is toughened and shrunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal agreement, such as an apprentice's, so a contract.

clue.text: Interrupt burglary

definitions.meaning: a forced entry into a building to steal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to butt in; as a noun it is a forced entry by a thief.

clue.text: Holding class to find new job for company leaver

indicators.note: the word for redeploying keeps the class letters inside it

parts.note: to reuse is to put to a new purpose
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a company finds work running a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company leaver' suggests a resigning employee; it means one who shuns company.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit withdraws from society, someone who leaves the company of others.

clue.text: Article on unusual lunar type of eclipse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: unusual signals the word lunar rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on a rare lunar eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped solar eclipse leaves a bright ring of sun, so this is one kind of eclipse.

clue.text: Black snake's opposite bag

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
in the board game Snakes and Ladders, the counterpart to a snake is a ladder

explanation.surface: A black snake lies across from a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake's opposite' points to Snakes and Ladders, the children's board game; the adder suggested by snake is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a membranous sac holding urine, a bag inside the body.

clue.text: Showed energy, holding extremely unpopular dance

indicators.note: the word for showed contains the letters picked out

parts.note: to bear is to show, as in bore a resemblance

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone full of energy performed a very unpopular dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showed' as BORE means displayed, as in bore a resemblance.
explanation.definitionFit: The bourrée is a lively French folk dance in duple time, an example of a dance.

clue.text: A major river's involved in producing industrial liquid

indicators.note: the river has the word in wrapped up inside it

parts.note: the Nile is a major river; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A great river's water is used to make an industrial chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniline is an oily liquid used to make dyes and plastics, an industrial chemical.

clue.text: Told rocket's first over the moon

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: over the moon means elated, delighted

explanation.surface: A rocket's first launch went over the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the moon' looks literal for a rocket; it is the idiom for delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell it, so related means told.

clue.text: Conforming to all the rules in healthy exercise

definitions.meaning: in line with a state's founding law or procedures
a walk taken for the sake of one's health

explanation.surface: Following every rule while taking a brisk walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lawful under a constitution; as a noun it is an old-fashioned word for a health walk.

clue.text: Not a very interesting Constable?

parts.note: read either as a boring policeman or as a lacklustre painting by John Constable, a grey sky being the joke

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means uninteresting and also grey or overcast, both fitting a tedious painting or officer.

clue.text: Quite badly injured on journey north — need this?

definitions.text: Quite badly injured on journey north — need this?

parts.note: a tour is a journey

indicators.note: the word Quite is damaged, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone seriously hurt while travelling north may need emergency first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: someone badly hurt on a trip may need this first-aid band.
explanation.definitionFit: A band tightened around a limb stops severe bleeding, exactly what a badly injured traveller may need.

clue.text: King's throat cut by enemy leader

indicators.note: the word for throat is split open by the letter inserted into it

parts.note: the gorge is an old word for the throat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An enemy commander slits a monarch's throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's' is the definition plus 'is'; George is a name of several British kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Six British monarchs have borne this name, so it is the name of a king.

clue.text: Always stop by front of rectory, where I live?

definitions.text: Always stop by front of rectory, where I live?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ever means always
an end is a stop

explanation.surface: A vicar asks the reader always to call at the rectory, their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places R beside EVER + END, ahead of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman such as a rector is styled this, and lives in the rectory.
